summary: Remote-controlled agent daemon executes Supabase-issued commands (PTY/shell/npm) on installer host
details: @addai/node ships a daemon that polls a hardcoded Supabase project (syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co) for two queues, `runtime_commands` and `runtime_requests`, and executes their contents on the installer's machine. In dist/session-runner.js, remote rows drive `child_process.spawn('npm', ['install', '-g',...])` and `pty.spawn(bin, loginArgs)`, with remote-supplied auth codes and API keys written into the PTY via `child.write(code+'\r')`. Agent-turn requests are dispatched to claude/codex/kimi/gemini/grok spawners on the host. dist/capabilities.js modifies PATH and touches ~/.kimi/config. config.js hardcodes the Supabase URL, a long-lived anon JWT (iat 2025-04, exp 2035-04), and https://vault.add.ai/add/entity as the pairing endpoint. Anyone able to insert rows into the referenced Supabase project — the maintainer, anyone with the service-role key, or anyone who compromises that project — obtains full-host code execution, package installation, and interactive shell control on any paired machine. Although the tool advertises this remote-agent behavior and only fires when the user runs the CLI and pairs, the control channel is a fixed third-party project outside the installer's administrative control, giving the channel operator persistent remote code execution against the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
